Yellow and white people: what is different?

Yellow = women. White with a black line = men.

Vocabulary: meaning

Register check

Some words for family are formal and informal.

Which words are formal? Which words are informal?

In the conversation, Liz says “Grandma” to her grandmother. Formal or informal?

Informal. Use informal words with friends and family. Use formal words at work.

FormalInformal

2C Complete the table

Singular (1 person)Plural (2+ people)
cousins
child

Track 1.18

Listen and check.

Look at the form

  • Most plurals add -s: cousin → cousins.
  • child → children is different.
  • wife → wives changes the ending.
  • Pairs: husband / wife, father / mother, son / daughter, brother / sister, uncle / aunt.

Liz = sister of Marcus. · Kyle = uncle of Liz. · Tim = cousin of Liz. · John = grandfather of Liz. · Anna = wife of Paul.

    Model answer: 2D
    • Anna is Liz’s mother. (Anna = mother of Liz.)
    • Paul is Liz’s father. (Paul = husband of Anna.)
    • Elizabeth is Liz’s grandmother.
    • Marcus is Liz’s brother. (Marcus = brother of Liz.)
    • Lisa is Liz’s aunt.

    Question and short answer: Is Kyle Liz’s uncle? Yes, he is.   Are John and Elizabeth Liz’s grandparents? Yes, they are.

    Highlight

    Task 2: highlight is, are, am and the short forms

    Short forms: ’s, ’re, ’m, isn’t
    Grammar: meaning

    What do is and are tell us?

    We use is and are to say who people are, how old they are, and how they are in a family.

    He’s my son. He’s eight. Who is “he”? How old is he?

    David. He is 8.

    She’s my daughter. She’s ten. One person or more than one?

    One person: Emily.

    Are your children here? One child or more than one?

    More than one.

    Is he your husband? Statement or question?

    A question. The answer is no: he’s Liz’s brother.

    My husband isn’t here. Is Liz’s husband at the party?

    No.

    Grammar: pronunciation

    Example: Are your children here? ↗   Yes, they are. ↘

    Freer practice

    4A Draw a simple family tree. Talk to a partner.

    Model:

    A: This is Marcos. He’s from Mexico City. He’s 25.

    B: Is he your brother?

    Ask and answer questions about the people in your family.

    Model answer: 4A

    Model talk about the tree:

    • A: This is Marcos. He’s from Mexico City. He’s 25.
    • B: Is he your brother?
    • A: Yes, he is. He’s my brother.
    • B: Is Sofia your sister?   A: Yes, she is. She’s 19.
    • B: Is Carlos your uncle?   A: No, he’s not. He’s my father.
    • B: Are Carlos and Rosa your parents?   A: Yes, they are.
    Freer practice

    4B Tell your group about three people

    Tell your group about three people from your family. You can show pictures of three people on your phone.

    Say

    This is …   He’s / She’s my …   He’s / She’s … (age).

    Ask and answer

    Is he your brother? Are they your children?
    Yes, he is. / No, he’s not. / Yes, they are.

    Vocabulary: pronunciation

    Sound focus: one rule at a time

    Rule 1/ʌ/ as in son. These words have the same vowel sound:

    sonmotherbrothercousinunclehusband

    Rule 2Weak ending /ɚ/: the last syllable is short and quiet.

    motherfatherbrothersisterdaughter

    Rule 3Daughter has silent letters: gh is not pronounced /ˈdɔːtɚ/.
